analysis.title: US Daily: What Does the Tightening in Financial Conditions Mean for Growth and the Fed?
key_insights: GS Financial Conditions Index has tightened about 100bp this year, all of it since early September, with over 40bp coming in the last week alone.

Main contributors are higher interest rates over the year plus the recent equity decline and dollar appreciation. Equities contribute even with the S&P 500 roughly flat because the index uses a price-earnings ratio and the ten-year average of earnings has risen.
If the tightening persists, GS estimates a 0.5pp drag on 2026Q4 GDP growth and 0.5pp on 2027 Q4/Q4 growth, a few tenths more than assumed in its 2027 forecast of 2.4% GDP growth.
If GS strategists' 2027 forecasts prove right (equity rebound, lower long-term rates), more than half of the tightening reverses and there is no additional drag beyond what is in the forecast.
A second 25bp hike in December is a near certainty, and GS still expects a third hike in March.

Reasons for the March hike: the tightening equals roughly 100bp of hikes and FOMC participants likely envision 75-100bp in total, part of the tightening reflects long rates pricing more hikes, and inflation is high with growth a bit above potential.

Contrast with 2016 and 2018 episodes when FCI tightening halted hikes. The Nov 2023 pause came when tightening was much larger than one additional hike would imply and was not driven by hike expectations.
Further tightening, especially from deteriorating risk sentiment or an AI spending pullback, could displace 2027 hikes. Some FOMC participants may project fewer hikes in the December dot plot.
AI demand is boosting core PCE inflation through cost spillovers and statistical mismeasurement, so an AI-led equity selloff could reduce the need for hikes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Equivalent to the usual impact of 100bp of rate hikes, a headwind to growth.
A few tenths more drag than assumed in GS forecasts if the tightening persists.
Baseline forecast already includes some financial conditions drag.

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp hike in December near certain, third hike in March expected
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hiking path continues unless risk sentiment deteriorates further.

risk_factors: Further FCI tightening led by risk sentiment deterioration could displace hikes and weigh on growth.
Concerns about a pullback in AI spending could drive an equity selloff.
Long-term rates driven by hike expectations may reverse if the FOMC does not follow through.
Persistent tightening adds a 0.5pp drag to 2027 growth.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows the GS US FCI tightening about 100bp since the start of 2026, with components including fed funds, 10y rate, credit spread, equities and exchange rate.
Exhibit 2 shows the real GDP growth impulse from the FCI under three scenarios: FCI at Nov. 19 level, FCI following GS strategist forecasts, and FCI at October FOMC level.
geopolitical: The FCI tightened meaningfully when the Iran war began but quickly reversed.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects a third hike in March because tightening matches intended hikes, inflation is high and growth is above potential.
tension_points.bear_case: Further tightening from weaker risk sentiment or an AI-led selloff could persuade the FOMC that more hikes are unnecessary.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further FCI tightening driven by risk sentiment deterioration independent of hike expectations, such as an AI-spending-led equity selloff.

theme_stances.key_argument: The tightening is not disproportionate to intended hikes and inflation is high, so GS keeps a March hike.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to expect a third hike in March
